podcast.body: A track from 1979 released on the Migraine label, serving as an example of the No Wave sound from the late 70s and early 80s. "This is called Burning Rubber from 1979."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.body: This track, featuring Lydia Lunch, is described as one of the more accessible songs from the avant-garde New York No Wave scene. Hearing it in 1978 would have been a "tough listen for most," marking it as distinct from bands like Van Halen or The Clash. "This is Teenage Jesus in the Jerks with their front person Lydia Lunch. It's called Burning Ruppar and it's one of the more accessible songs from the scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
